channel.title: AI Threat Watch: LLMjacking
channel.description: Verified case files in the category LLMjacking.

item.title: [CRITICAL] PoeLLM botnet infects 3,400 servers running exposed LiteLLM and Ollama for cryptomining
item.description: Lumen Black Lotus Labs tracked an ELF implant named libgcrypt that derives its C2 address from words in a GitHub-hosted poem, scans ports 3000 and 4000, exploits LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 and runs XMRig and Iron miners on more than 3,400 hosts. Target: Exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] GTG-50021: fake discounted-Claude reseller proxied traffic and stole Anthropic credentials
item.description: A Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking group sold cheap Claude access, silently routed buyers to other models and ran a credential harvester that captured Anthropic account logins for resale. Target: Customers buying discounted Claude access. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Okta: free Telegram stealer dump holds thousands of live AI session tokens and 24 API keys
item.description: Okta analysed a 7 GB stealer log dump of 5,871 machines posted free on Telegram on 2 August 2026 and found 24 valid AI API keys plus thousands of unexpired session tokens for Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and Amazon. Target: Users of Google, Microsoft, Anthropic, Amazon and OpenAI AI. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] 15 JetBrains Marketplace AI plugins with 70,000 installs steal OpenAI and DeepSeek keys
item.description: Aikido found at least 15 plugins from seven vendor accounts that acted as AI assistants but sent users OpenAI, DeepSeek and SiliconFlow API keys over plain HTTP to an attacker server; a paid tier gave out harvested keys. Target: Developers using JetBrains IDE AI assistant plugins. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Hijacked Ollama server used as brain of autonomous hacking pipeline
item.description: Sysdig observed an attacker using an unauthenticated Ollama instance as the reasoning engine of a tool that scanned targets, wrote exploits and attempted intrusions. Target: Exposed Ollama servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] PRC clusters UNC5673 and UNC6201 pooled Gemini, Claude and OpenAI accounts via proxies
item.description: GTIG found UNC5673 (overlapping TEMP.Hex) using Claude-Relay-Service and CLI-Proxy-API to share pooled accounts, and UNC6201 trialling a script that auto-registers premium LLM accounts with CAPTCHA and SMS bypass. Target: Frontier model providers' account and billing controls. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Cybernews: 45 of 98 unauthenticated Open WebUI servers already running miners and stealers
item.description: Cybernews researchers found 98 Open WebUI servers with authentication disabled and over 2,000 allowing open sign-up; 45 of the unauthenticated hosts carried a cryptominer and infostealer operation seen in 14 variants with Discord webhook alerts. Target: Exposed Open WebUI instances. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Operation Bizarre Bazaar: hijacked LLM endpoints resold through commercial marketplace
item.description: Pillar Security logged ~35,000 attack sessions scanning for exposed AI endpoints, validating access and reselling it via a marketplace covering 30+ LLM providers. Target: Exposed Ollama, vLLM and MCP endpoints. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] ShadowRay 2.0 turns exposed Ray AI clusters into self-spreading mining botnet
item.description: Oligo reported attackers abusing unauthenticated Ray job APIs (CVE-2023-48022) with LLM-written payloads to hijack AI GPU clusters for cryptomining, DDoS and data theft. Target: Ray (Anyscale) AI compute clusters. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Exposed Open WebUI instance hijacked to run AI-generated cryptominer and infostealer
item.description: Sysdig observed an attacker abuse an Open WebUI server exposed with admin rights and no login, uploading an obfuscated, partly AI-written Python Tool that deployed XMRig and T-Rex miners on Linux and Java infostealers on Windows. Target: Internet-exposed Open WebUI deployment. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Microsoft names Storm-2139 members who hijacked Azure OpenAI with stolen keys
item.description: Microsoft amended its lawsuit to name four people in a ring that used scraped customer API keys to access Azure OpenAI, bypass guardrails, resell access and generate harmful imagery. Target: Microsoft Azure OpenAI customers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] LLMjacking crews load stolen DeepSeek keys into reverse proxies days after model launch
item.description: Sysdig found over 20 reverse proxies running on stolen credentials; one held 55 DeepSeek keys, another burned 2.2 billion tokens worth tens of thousands of dollars in 4.5 days and resold access for 30 USD a month. Target: Cloud and AI API account holders (OpenAI, AWS, Azure). GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] DeepSeek halts new sign-ups after month-long DDoS and brute-force campaign peaks
item.description: DeepSeek said its services were under large-scale malicious attack on 28 January 2025 and limited sign-ups to Chinese mobile numbers; Qi An Xin XLab traced a month of escalating DDoS and brute-force traffic. Target: DeepSeek chat and API services. CN. Verification: confirmed.
